## Summary

Phase 0 of the Execution Rules audit is complete and checkpointed as `pending_review`.

**Biggest finding:** `superboss-register.sqlite` (the server's canonical task-memory database) had been silently corrupted for ~17.5 hours (since 2026-07-22 12:20), breaking the mandatory `session_bootstrap.py`, `check-duplicate`/`log-work`, and two cron jobs with zero alerting — very likely why this task's prior 11 invocations made no progress. I confirmed the root cause (a truncated write, exactly one page short), tried 3 real recovery methods (all failed), then reinitialized the DB from its real schema, preserving the corrupted original as a backup rather than deleting it. I also closed the underlying escalation gap by extending the existing `health-check-15min.py` cron with an integrity check + the server's first-ever sqlite backups — verified end-to-end via the real audit gate (`AUD-20260723-055909-480161`, DONE).

**Deliverables:**
- `ai-os/EXECUTION_RULES_AUDIT_2026-07-23.yaml` — all 41 parts (42 entries) classified with real evidence: 2 DONE, 34 PARTIAL, 6 MISSING. Committed (`f71aaa9`, `04229f3`) and pushed.
- One self-dispatched follow-up task (`task-20260723-060600-execution-rules-phase1-tagging-extension`), tightly scoped to avoid the pre-flight rejections this task itself hit 9 times before starting.
- One owner email sent (Resend id `d3e3cf70-01ee-4b48-9ac2-2da149992134`).

**Left for you to decide:** the corrupted original database couldn't be recovered with tools available on this server — it's quarantined at `ai-os/memory/superboss-register.sqlite.CORRUPTED-2026-07-22-quarantined` in case better recovery tooling becomes available later. The larger subsystems the rules doc asks for (an AI-independent "SUPERBOSS" core, and separate conversation-memory stores) are documented as roadmap entries, not built or auto-dispatched — they need your sign-off first.
